pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - The strongest support is balance sheet capacity: net debt is 1.32x reported EBITDA and cover is 10.79x, so at today's net debt earnings could fall by 43.39% before leverage returned to the 2.34x of fiscal 2025. No debt matures before fiscal 2030, and USD 665.0 million of the revolver is undrawn before letters of credit alongside USD 256.0 million of cash, so there is no refinancing need or liquidity squeeze in the next two years. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C8; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Cash generation is solid but flattered by tax timing. Free cash flow was 85.57% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and capital expenditure took 10.61% of operating cash flow, yet deferred taxes meant that part of the tax expense was not paid in cash, and free cash flow after deferred taxes is 80.19% of EBITDA, so durable conversion is nearer four fifths than the headline. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The weakest dimension is earnings concentration in rate-linked custodial revenue, which is 49.66% of first-half revenue and 63.49% of gross profit at a 93.22% gross margin, with partners that hold the cash paying fees equal to about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue. A fall of 43.39% in EBITDA, equal to 32.96% of custodial revenue with no cost saving, would be needed to return net leverage to the fiscal 2025 level, so the exposure is large in earnings terms but far from distressing leverage. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C8; calculation C9; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The franchise supports revenue visibility but not pricing power. HSAs grew 8% in the year to July 31, 2026, accounts belong to members and carry closure fees, and retention is described as strong, while average service fees per account and the average card interchange rate both fell, and the yield on HSA cash rose 32 bp to 3.83% as lower-yield contracts repriced. Volume, not price, drives growth outside custodial yield. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C20

- Financial policy is the second constraint and is mixed rather than adverse. Repurchases were 73.24% of free cash flow in fiscal 2026 and 114.60% in the first half of fiscal 2027, USD 948.4 million of authorization remains, which is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and net debt rose while the revolver was still reduced. The board can stop repurchases at any time, which is the main management lever, and sponsor and governance risk is Medium on the earlier assessment. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C22; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Refinancing is a single-year question. The whole USD 935.0 million of principal falls due in fiscal 2030, with the revolver and the notes 39 days apart, and the notes are redeemable at par since October 1, 2026; their fair value is 97.17% of principal, a Level 2 estimate. No rating or market price series is supplied, so market access is judged from the maturity profile and low leverage alone, and the issue becomes live in fiscal 2029. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 107; calculation C14; calculation C15; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The primary downside path runs from lower interest rates and equity prices to custodial and investment-fee income, and the monitor is the yield on repricing HSA cash against the 3.9% book average. Treasury bond forwards hedge part of future placements but carry a net liability of USD 85,198 thousand, 9.25% of liquidity, so the hedge is a liability today and becomes protection only if rates fall. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C13; calculation C16

runs.text: - Strength: low leverage and long-dated debt. Net debt is 1.32x EBITDA and cover is 10.79x, which lets earnings absorb a large fall before leverage reaches the fiscal 2025 level, and no principal is due until fiscal 2030, so default risk from refinancing or liquidity is low for the next two years. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Strength: sticky, member-owned accounts with low capital needs. HSAs belong to members and carry closure fees, retention is strong on the company's account, and capital expenditure took 10.61% of operating cash flow, so account growth converts to cash that services debt. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C6

- Strength: cost efficiency in the service line. Service costs fell 7% while service revenue rose 4%, lifting service gross margin by 7.41 percentage points, which cushions the margin if revenue growth slows. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C10

- Weakness: earnings concentration in rate-linked custodial revenue. It is 63.49% of gross profit, partners paying the yield supply about 48% of revenue, and each 10% fall removes 13.16% of EBITDA, so a falling-rate cycle would hit the largest profit pool first. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C7; calculation C9

- Weakness: capital return above cash generation. Repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow in the first half, authorization remaining is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and the revolver is the funding backstop, so leverage can rise without any earnings fall. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C17; calculation C18

- Weakness: a single maturity year and floating-rate revolver. All principal falls due within 39 days in 2029, and the revolver floats at 5.08%, so a closed market in 2029 would hit the whole stack at once, although a one percent rate rise costs only about USD 3.4 million a year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation C14; calculation C21

runs.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or new debt issue is pending or described in the supplied filings after the quarter ended July 31, 2026, and the run settings name no transaction, so this section records the completed transactions that shape the creditor position. The latest debt financing is the five-year senior secured revolving credit facility of up to USD 1.0 billion entered on August 23, 2024, which refinanced the prior credit agreement, the facility under which the BenefitWallet purchase had been funded. USD 335.0 million is drawn at July 31, 2026, alongside USD 600 million of 4.50% senior notes due 2029 issued in October 2021. Basis: 10-K_2026-01-31_hqy-20260131.htm.jsonl, pages 107–108; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-07-31_hqy-20260731.htm.jsonl, pages 6–20

The BenefitWallet HSA portfolio, bought for USD 425.0 million with USD 2.7 billion of HSA Assets, closed in three tranches between March and May 2024 and was paid with USD 225.0 million of revolver borrowings and USD 200.0 million of cash. The board has since raised the repurchase authorization twice, in June 2025 and May 2026, to USD 1.6 billion in all, and the filings describe no borrowing to fund repurchases. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: HealthEquity is a scaled, listed HSA custodian with no sponsor or controlling holder named, so creditors face little ownership-driven extraction risk, but nearly half of revenue and most gross profit come from interest-linked custodial fees, and latest-half buybacks exceeded free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The franchise is large, with HSA Assets of USD 37.9 billion at July 31, 2026, and no customer provides more than 10% of revenue. The board added USD 1.0 billion to the repurchase authorization in May 2026, and first-half repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow while cash fell. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: it would rise if buybacks were funded from the revolver and fall if the proxy statement confirms independent oversight.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The business is a recurring-fee franchise rather than a transaction-driven one, which supports revenue visibility. The company holds HSA Assets of USD 37.9 billion for its members, reports about 20% of the HSA market by assets, says most accounts open before each fiscal year starts, and has no customer above 10% of revenue. The market share figure is a company statement citing an industry report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings depend on interest rates and a small set of partners. Custodial revenue is 49.66% of first-half revenue and 63.49% of gross profit, and fees from insurance company and depository partners were about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue, up from 39% in fiscal 2024. USD 2.3 billion of HSA cash earning 1.5% reprices in the rest of fiscal 2027, against a book average of 3.9%, so custodial income follows the rates at which cash reprices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Asset growth is coming from invested balances, not cash, which makes fee income market-sensitive. HSA investments are 54.20% of HSA Assets against 45.70% at January 31, 2025, and grew 28% in the year to July 31, 2026 while HSA cash grew 2%. Invested balances earn fees set as a percentage of the balance, so a market fall would cut service fees while the cash that earns custodial revenue is nearly flat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sponsor, parent or controlling holder appears in the supplied filings, so there is no documented sponsor fee, dividend recapitalisation or exit channel, and the company has no current plans to pay dividends. The company reports 19 holders of record, not counting holders in street name, the percentage held by any holder is not stated, and ownership, director independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so low extraction risk rests on absence of disclosure.

fields.value: - Financial policy has moved from returns funded by free cash flow to returns above it, a mixed rather than extractive pattern. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Audit and reporting quality are adequate for creditor monitoring, with one open item. The auditor stated that the statements present fairly and that internal control was effective, the chair is separate from the chief executive, and a board committee oversees cybersecurity. The cybersecurity litigation has no loss estimate or accrual and its description narrowed between the 2025 and 2026 annual reports without explanation, so that exposure is unquantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a low-risk reading is that capital return has outrun cash generation. First-half repurchases were 114.60% of free cash flow, the new authorization is 2.17x last-twelve-months free cash flow, and the revolver that funded the 2024 acquisition is also the stated source for further acquisitions. The view would move to High if repurchases were funded by revolver draws, if a dividend were introduced, or if the credit agreement proved to allow wide distributions.

fields.value: Fundamental credit for Healthequity, Inc. (issuer id hqy-1428336), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: HealthEquity is a low-leverage credit with no debt due before fiscal 2030, so creditors face little near-term risk, but earnings tied to interest rates and buybacks that exceeded free cash flow in the latest half are the pressure points.

fields.value: Reported net debt is 1.32x last-twelve-months EBITDA and interest cover is 10.79x. Custodial revenue, which follows interest rates, supplies 63.49% of gross profit, so a 10% fall in it with no cost saving would remove 13.16% of EBITDA. The view would weaken if buybacks were funded from the revolver and strengthen if free cash flow again exceeds them.

No debt matures before fiscal 2030, and USD 665.0 million of the revolver is undrawn before letters of credit alongside USD 256.0 million of cash, so there is no refinancing need or liquidity squeeze in the next two years.

fields.value: HealthEquity administers consumer health savings accounts and other consumer-directed benefits and earns service fees, custodial yield on HSA cash and card interchange. Its credit relevance is that most accounts are opened before each fiscal year begins, which gives revenue visibility, while custodial yield makes about half of revenue sensitive to interest rates. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is largely recurring and account-driven: service fees are fixed tiered fees paid monthly for the term of the client agreement, custodial revenue is yield on HSA cash and client-held funds, and interchange follows card spending and is the only transactional line at 15.27% of first-half revenue. Volume is rising, with HSAs up 8% and new HSAs from sales up 20% in the first half of fiscal 2027, while other benefit accounts fell 2%. Pricing power is mixed: the average yield on HSA cash rose from 3.51% to 3.83% as contracts repriced to higher yields, but average service fees per account and the average interchange rate both fell. Switching costs are high because accounts belong to the member and closure fees apply, retention is described as strong and no churn rate is disclosed. Revenue is therefore predictable in the service and custodial lines, rate-driven in custodial, regulated throughout because tax law creates the product, and not structurally declining.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of revenue was 27.1% of revenue in the first half of fiscal 2027 against 30.4% a year earlier, because service costs fell 7% on technology efficiencies and lower fraud reimbursements, medical claims and consulting spend while revenue rose 7%; service gross margin rose by 7.41 percentage points to 38.76%. Custodial costs are small at 6.78% of custodial revenue, so custodial income reaches EBITDA almost in full. Operating expenses before amortization and integration rose 13.21% against revenue growth of 7.42%, led by technology and general and administrative spend, so part of the gross margin gain is being spent. Reported EBITDA margin was 39.98% in the first half against 38.06%. Stock-based compensation was 15.30% of fiscal 2026 reported EBITDA, which is why the issuer's adjusted EBITDA is 18.53% higher. Margins can be defended against volume pressure, but not against a custodial yield fall, because custodial costs are small and do not fall with the revenue, so the loss reaches EBITDA directly.

fields.value: Capital needs are small: capital expenditure was 10.61% of operating cash flow in fiscal 2026 and is expected to stay at the same level in fiscal 2027, mainly software. Free cash flow was 85.57% of reported EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and 85.75% over the last twelve months, but part of that is tax timing: deferred taxes of USD 28,340 thousand over the period were expense not paid in cash, and the company says the 2025 tax act accelerated deductions so that cash taxes in fiscal 2027 are expected to be significantly reduced, although first-half cash taxes were USD 35,586 thousand against USD 6,507 thousand a year earlier. After removing deferred taxes conversion is 80.19%. Costs of new accounts are incurred in the third and fourth quarters before the revenue arrives, so quarter-end leverage is seasonal. Free cash flow covers cash interest of USD 47,233 thousand over the last twelve months 9.25 times, which leaves room to service the debt and fund buybacks, and capital expenditure could be trimmed to protect cash, although the company plans to keep it level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and asymmetric: banks such as Optum Bank and Webster Bank and retail investment companies such as Fidelity Investments compete for HSAs with greater resources, and Fidelity has gained significant share, so competition can limit service pricing and obliges the company to offer competitive yields to keep members. New entrants need Treasury approval as a non-bank custodian or a bank charter, which has not stopped well-resourced entrants. Substitution comes from network partners that decide to offer HSAs directly, which the company says would reduce channel opportunities and cause attrition, and from policy change such as single payer proposals. Buyer power is moderate because no customer exceeds 10% of revenue and switching an HSA takes effort and may cost closure fees. Supplier power is the force that matters most for credit: insurance company and depository partners paid fees equal to about 48% of fiscal 2026 revenue and set the yield, one bank identification number sponsor supports the card programme, and one custodial investment partner holds invested balances, none of them named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and economic factors are material to credit. HSA products exist because of tax law, the 2025 tax act widened HSA eligibility to Bronze and Catastrophic plans, and the company also says proposals to curtail HSAs or move to single payer could harm the business. Interest rates and equity markets set custodial yield and invested balances. Social and cost trends support demand: the company cites average family health insurance premiums up 26% since 2020, which increases cost sharing and HSA take-up. Technology matters through service-cost efficiency from technology investment and artificial intelligence tools, and through the 2024 cybersecurity incident whose litigation has no loss estimate.

fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the company's stated expectation that yield on HSA cash rises further if rates hold, account growth with HSAs up 8%, wider HSA eligibility and continued service-cost efficiency; the headwinds are a possible fall in market rates, operating expenses growing faster than revenue, cash taxes that could rise towards the tax expense once accelerated deductions run off, which the filings do not schedule, and the open litigation. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside is a falling-rate and falling-equity cycle. The first break is custodial revenue: new and repriced HSA cash earns less, client-held funds reprice immediately, and invested balances, now 54.20% of HSA Assets (calculation C24), fall in value and cut service fees. Because custodial costs are only 6.78% of custodial revenue, the loss reaches EBITDA almost in full; each 10% fall in custodial revenue removes USD 67,073.9 thousand, or 13.16% of EBITDA, and takes net leverage to 1.53x and cover to 9.37x with no cost saving. Free cash flow falls by a similar amount before tax while buybacks of USD 231,054 thousand in a half-year continue unless the board stops them, and the Treasury bond forwards settle in cash from August 2026 with a net liability of USD 85,198 thousand. Liquidity of USD 921,003 thousand before letters of credit and no maturity before fiscal 2030 mean there is no refinancing or liquidity event in the next two years; EBITDA would have to fall 43.39%, a custodial revenue fall of 32.96%, before leverage returned to the fiscal 2025 level. Management levers are suspending buybacks, trimming capital expenditure and the undrawn revolver, and resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the observable triggers are the yield on repricing HSA cash, HSA cash growth, repurchases against free cash flow and the revolver balance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, HealthEquity presents a strong business profile in scale and account stickiness, but credit quality is constrained by earnings concentrated in rate-linked custodial revenue and by buybacks that exceeded free cash flow in the latest half. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: free cash flow converts 85.57% of EBITDA, though 80.19% after deferred taxes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on leverage staying low and on the market in 2029, when the whole USD 935.0 million falls due. The primary downside path is lower rates and equity prices cutting custodial and fee income while buybacks continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the proxy statement, the yield on repricing cash, partner terms, a rating or price series and any later filing. Top risk: custodial income compression with buybacks funded from the revolver.
